content:
alex (cust)-AcmeRetail: hey, getting a bunch of 413s when we try to upload a large batch of texts to /v1/embeddings. Happens when we switch to streaming/chunked uploads. payload size ~12MB, single request.

tess (Support): sorry to hear that — thanks for the details. can you paste the raw curl you used (with creds redacted) and the exact 413 response body? also which region / api host?

alex (cust)-AcmeRetail: curl is basically: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d @batch.json
```
batch.json is an array of ~60k short strings (~200 tokens avg). response body is short: `{\"error\":\"Payload too large\",\"code\":413}` sometimes we see `nginx 413` in front of that. region: us-west-2.

sev-bot: Incident created: #87654 - 413s on embeddings bulk upload (ticket: 2026-03-14-87654) :rotating_light:

sanjay (Infra): tagging in. quick note: many infra layers choke on either Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding: chunked. proxys and wafs often have client_max_body_size or max_request_body_size configs. do you send Transfer-Encoding: chunked or a Content-Length header?

alex (cust)-AcmeRetail: we tried both. node client uses `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` in streaming mode. when we switch to single POST with Content-Length it also 413s but less frequently. seems related to request size.

maya (ML Eng): also worth checking: are you building the JSON by concatenation? if there's a stray comma/encoding issue we might cause the downstream parser to allocate more memory or mis-parse arrays which could trigger rejection. but 413 is size-related.

tess (Support): immediate mitigation: try reducing per-request batch size to ~1000 texts (or smaller) and retry. we have a soft recommended payload limit documented ~1MB-5MB per request depending on region/load. also try `Content-Encoding: gzip` to compress payloads.

alex (cust)-AcmeRetail: small batches work fine. but we need throughput, so chunking into tiny pieces kills latency. curious if streaming/chunked should be supported for large batches? your docs mention streaming for generation, not bulk embeddings.

sanjay (Infra): short answer: streaming/chunked upload to the embeddings endpoint is supported in the sense of TCP chunking, but many upstream components (load balancers, WAF, reverse proxies) have limits that can reject large sustained chunked streams. some gateways compute an internal size and enforce a maximum (e.g., 8MB). nginx default `client_max_body_size` is 1MB in some builds; we have custom settings but cloud LB rules can still interfere.

sanjay (Infra): debug questions for reproducible repro: 1) can you share the exact request headers (minus auth)? 2) can you reproduce with `curl --libcurl dump.c` or `curl --verbose --compressed`? 3) does the failure correlate with particular CL values or times of day?

alex (cust)-AcmeRetail: header dump: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood-inference.com
Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]
Content-Type: application/json
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
User-Agent: node-fetch/2.6
```
response headers when 413: `server: nginx`, `content-length: 54`, body: `{\"error\":\"Payload too large\"}`

maya (ML Eng): another potential pitfall when streaming large embedding batches: if you do on-the-fly tokenization and piecewise dimension packing you can accidentally produce arrays with inconsistent embedding dims. the client should validate vector length before sending. sample server error we want to avoid: `embedding dimension mismatch (expected 1536, got 1535)` — but that's separate from 413.

ops-triage: note: there's also an edge-case where chunked uploads + gzip + some LBs strip the `Transfer-Encoding` header and re-evaluate request size leading to 413. can you try turning off gzip for a quick test?

alex (cust)-AcmeRetail: disabled gzip, still 413 in ~25% of requests. switching to Content-Length header with a single big POST gives 413 ~60% of time. small batches never fail.

sanjay (Infra): ok we reproduced something similar in staging with a simulated 12MB JSON stream and our edge LB. reproduction notes we logged: LB (haproxy) drops chunked body if a backend returns a 502, but more importantly it enforces `tune.options.httpchk` size limit. working theory: our edge LB is treating some chunk sequences as exceeding the configured `req.body` cap. we'll open a config change task but that requires rollout and testing.

tess (Support): temporary workaround for customers: 1) batch size reduction (we know it hurts throughput) 2) gzip compression + smaller chunks 3) upload a gzipped NDJSON file to S3 and call our ingestion endpoint with an S3 pointer (we have a server-side ingestion job that can read from S3 for large datasets). if you want, we can arrange a one-off S3 ingestion so you can keep throughput.

alex (cust)-AcmeRetail: S3 ingestion would work. what are the steps? is that an enterprise-only flow?

tess (Support): we support S3 ingestion for Dedicated/Private customers by default; for Hosted we have a quick adhoc pipeline. I'll spin up a support ticket and an ops runbook. need: (1) S3 bucket with putObject prefix, (2) ephemeral creds we give you, (3) confirm NDJSON format with one text per line and metadata like `id` and `text`. I'll DM you the template and follow-up.

maya (ML Eng): follow-up engineering items: - add a clearer 413 response with hint about chunked vs content-length and recommended per-request payload maximum - add a doc section on streaming/chunked upload caveats and recommended chunk size & compression - investigate allowing a streaming-id header so clients can do resumable chunked uploads (longer term)

sanjay (Infra): ops task created: INF-9282 update LB body size thresholds + add metrics to track `413_by_route`. pushing to triage for next deploy window.

ops-triage: action item for support: offer S3 ingestion or suggest client-side batching and `Content-Encoding: gzip`. for immediate unblock we can also whitelist the customer's IP on LB for a short window while they finish an initial bulk load.

alex (cust)-AcmeRetail: will do S3 ingestion. thanks for the quick help. please keep me posted on that LB change — we want streaming eventually but need the immediate data load.

sev-bot: update: ticket #87654 assigned to infra (sanjay), ETA initial patch in 48h.

tess (Support): closing loop notes for the thread: immediate mitigations provided (S3 ingestion or reduce per-request size or gzip), infra on LB investigation, doc update assigned to maya. i'll attach the NDJSON template and a short script to chunk batches safely. :white_check_mark:

alex (cust)-AcmeRetail: appreciated. small note for docs: explicitly call out that embeddings endpoint may experience 413s with chunked uploads due to intermediate proxies — that would have saved us time.

maya (ML Eng): agreed — will draft a short "bulk upload best practices" doc and include a recommended `chunk_size` example and sample Node/Go upload patterns.

sanjay (Infra): leaving a quick repro snippet we used in staging: 
```bash
python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.dumps([{'id':i,'text':'x'*1500} for i in range(6000)]))" > big.json
curl -v -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' -X POST https://staging-api.example.local/v1/embeddings --data-binary @big.json
```
we saw `413` from the LB before the backend even saw the request.

alex (cust)-AcmeRetail: thanks everyone. i'll follow-up in dm for S3 creds.
